fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Tropical Versus Sidereal Question, Answered In The Actual Sky", "body": "PK says it took him roughly a year to work out what the difference between tropical and sidereal astrology actually is, and he came on Vibe Rant to explain it the way he never heard anyone else explain it. Rather than a flat chart pulled off a website, he screen shares the free desktop version of Stellarium, which he argues is far better than the phone app, and walks the ecliptic degree by degree. His anchor point: the spring equinox, zero degrees tropical Aries, sits right below the right fish of the constellation Pisces, and will stay there for your grandkids."}, {"title": "Four Minutes A Day: The Mechanics Behind The Signs", "body": "The engine of the whole episode is a small number. PK demonstrates in Stellarium that a sidereal day, one full turn of the background stars, runs about four minutes ahead of a solar day, so the sun appears to precess backwards through the ecliptic and the signs change. He then takes on the claim, which he credits to Crow, that the equinox has nothing to do with equal day and night, arguing that any measurement depends on atmosphere and on where you decide first light begins, so the published figures land days off the equinox itself."}, {"title": "Springtime Is Springtime: Chance On Signs As Language", "body": "Invited to weigh in, Chance Garton argues the tropical and sidereal fight gets conflated with heliocentrism when the cosmology is beside the point. Whatever model you imagine, the equinox marks entry into spring, the plants and the weather do what they do. He contends the constellations were given their names and descriptions to match the twelve thirty degree segments as an allegorical teaching tool for the order of the year, so the systems are languages rather than rivals. PK agrees, comparing the debate to arguing over which language is better when both convey the same idea, and both liken astrology to tarot."}, {"title": "Gabe's Weaves: Caligula, Plato's Divided Line And The Hostage Shot", "body": "Slick Dissident brings four long tangents. He reads the Taurus pileup as a reenactment of Caligula ordering his soldiers to make war on the sea and gather seashells in their helmets, which he calls a curse designed to break the spirit of fighting men, citing the French escargot as an insult buried in language. He proposes one reading of Plato's Republic, exactly twelve hours, as the true measure of half a day. He ties the torch of the summer solstice to Hymenaios, cherub of receptivity and wedding vows, and reads the autumn equinox line over Virgo's shoulder as the hostage rescue shot he teaches in firearms training."}, {"title": "Precession You Cannot Measure, And The Purple Posies Deferred", "body": "In the last stretch PK argues the one degree per seventy two years figure is an average built on wobble, something three generations of diligent surveys still could not verify, and warns against treating mathematical equations as reality even while running a program built from them. He shows Mars and Jupiter turning retrograde, the wandering stars, and the IAU constellation borders that make true sidereal signs unequal. Gabe finds the IAU acronym mirrored in the Greek numeral for nine hundred eleven and keeps landing Urania in the ninth spot. Apollo's purple posies got bumped to a future Wednesday."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tonight we call to the stage one of our favorite syncro-weavers from the Telegram community, PK! Subjects on the docket include using Stellarium to grasp celestial mechanics, by looking at the equinoxes & solstices and zodiac signs, we may just make sense of the sidereal vs. tropical question. After that we'll start pulling the purple thread in mysticism, considering ancient authors, the myth of Apollo & Hyacinth, and more. Definitely going to be jam packed with gravy!
